title: Patchwave degradation and capacity recovery plan — June 2026
content:
Purpose:
This is the operational plan for the June 2026 patchwave targeting GPU driver and microcode updates across our multi-region fleet. The goal is to perform a staged driver upgrade while keeping user-visible token latency within SLO targets and limiting net capacity loss to <12% per region at peak. This doc contains the proposed drain windows, stepped rollback-safe procedures, surge buffer allocations, and validation checks.

Background/context:
- We need to apply driver 528.45 and a firmware micro-patch to mitigate a determinism bug impacting certain A100 batches under long-lived KV cache usage.
- Canary runs on a small Canaries pool showed 0.6% increased p99 latency but no correctness regressions. Larger rollout will expose transient memory fragmentation that requires staggered drains and targeted warm-up.
- Past upgrades (Mar 2026) used 30% single-window drains and resulted in queueing spikes in EU-west. We will avoid that pattern.

Scope and constraints:
- Regions in-scope: us-west1, us-east4, eu-west2, ap-northeast1.
- Hardware: mixed A100-40GB and A100-80GB clusters (SKU tags: a100-40, a100-80).
- No maintenance on private customer-dedicated racks during their blackout windows (see customer calendar).
- Work must be completed within June 7–20 maintenance window to meet compliance deadlines.

Execution windows (proposed):
- Phase 0 (Canary verification): 2026-06-07 02:00–06:00 UTC — us-west1 canaries only (5% fleet).
- Phase 1 (Wave A): 2026-06-09 00:00–08:00 UTC — us-west1 and us-east4, staggered per cell.
- Phase 2 (Wave B): 2026-06-12 00:00–10:00 UTC — eu-west2 (longer warm-up).
- Phase 3 (Wave C): 2026-06-16 02:00–12:00 UTC — ap-northeast1 (time-zone friendly).
- Roll-forward buffer days: 2026-06-17–20 for any unanticipated retries.

Per-region drain targets and rationale:
- us-west1: target 18% drained per cell, but we will keep 2x canary machines online for fast fallback. This region has highest spare capacity.
- us-east4: target 12% drained; due to heavy traffic peaks we limit drain size and increase batching to keep TCO.
- eu-west2: target 20% drained with extended warm-up because of prior memory fragmentation sensitivity.
- ap-northeast1: target 15% drained; longer sequencing to avoid local spikes.

Capacity math (quick):
- Fleet totals (logical): us-west1=250 GPUs, us-east4=180, eu-west2=140, ap-northeast1=120.
- Planned transient reduction (max): us-west1=45, us-east4=22, eu-west2=28, ap-northeast1=18.
- Global spare buffer: reserve 60 GPUs from Dedicated burst pool and scale up ephemeral hosts if autoscaling thresholds breach 65% util.

Prechecks (must be green before each wave):
1) Canary health (latency/throughput) — rolling 1h p95/p99 within +15% of baseline.
2) KV cache hit rate within expected variance.
3) Host-level metrics: memory pressure <70%, GPU temperature nominal, no ECC errors in last 24h.
4) Observability ingestion healthy (no >30s telemetry gaps).
5) Communication confirmations from on-call, customer success, and compute provisioning.

Drain & patch steps (per cell):
1) Mark cell into maintenance mode in the console: set route-policy=degraded and pause new long-running sessions.
2) Graceful drain: schedule active requests to finish with soft cutoff of 20s for start-of-request queuing. Use continuous-batching hold for 90s, then start instance-level graceful shutdown.
3) Evacuate KV caches to nearest warm hosts using kv-redis offload tool and pre-warm target hosts with synthetic prompts.
4) Apply driver and firmware patch to machine. Reboot host.
5) Smoke test model: run golden prompt set (10 prompts, assertions on token differences and latency band).
6) Rejoin host: return to pool in warm-up mode (traffic at 10% for 10 min, 30% for 20 min, then 100%). Monitor memory fragmentation and p99.
7) If smoke tests fail or p99 > +40% baseline for longer than 10m, immediately rollback: revert driver via image snapshot and rebootstrap from last-known-good image, mark cell as degraded, escalate to infra-ops.

Driver/patch specifics:
- Target driver: nvidia/528.45. Fixes determinism in kernel 3c.
- Firmware micro-patch: fw-2026-04a (non-disruptive except reboot).
- Rollback plan: maintain snapshot images for immediate revert (image-tag: prepatch-2026-06-xx). Testing will verify snapshot restore cycle <22 minutes.

Fallback and surge strategy:
- If region-wide p99 breach persists >30m despite rollback attempts, engage cross-region routing: shift 10–15% of traffic to alternate region with compatible model variant. Use smart routing policy: latency-first, cost-second.
- Dedicated reserved burst pool: allocate 60 GPUs (from Dedicated) for emergency capacity. Pre-authorize reserve usage via finance flag.
- Autoscaler config: temporary scale-up threshold lowered to 55% util for the maintenance window to trigger earlier provisioning.

Observability and verification checklist (automated + manual):
- Automated: Prometheus alerts: gpu.memory.fragmentation, model.p99, queue.length. Dashboards: per-cell heatmap, KV cache hit-rate.
- Manual: Run load tests (50 QPS synthetic) against a single patched host before full rejoin. Confirm token-cost delta <2% and quality regression alert shows 0 failures.
- Logging retention: keep detailed driver logs for 72 hours post-patch.

Communication plan:
- Pre-window: 48h customer-stellar notice (CS to send), announce on #infra-maintenance Slack channel and post schedule to Confluence.
- During window: designated incident channel #infra-patchwave-2026 and on-call rotations: primary (Marcus Nguyen), secondary (Ravi Patel), exec updates by 30m cadence if any region >threshold.
- Post-window: summary note to #infra-maintenance, tag affected product owners and update Confluence timeline.

Post-maintenance validation (T+1 day):
- Run full regression suite for top-10 models and sample production prompts.
- Verify cost delta and token-per-call metrics.
- Confirm no ECC or hardware reboots beyond expected.

Estimated customer impact and mitigation:
- Expected transient increase in p99 up to +12% in impacted cells during warm-up. Mitigations: staggered drains, increased batching, and cross-region routing.
- Expected SLA exposure: small risk window for SLOs in eu-west2; prepare crediting playbook if SLA breach triggered.

Action items & owners (short):
- Finalize canary dataset and golden prompts — Olivia Chen (due 2026-06-05).
- Pre-stage rollback images and verify restore time — Marcus Nguyen (due 2026-06-06).
- Confirm Dedicated burst pool allocation and finance flag — Leah Thompson (due 2026-06-04).
- CS customer blackout cross-check — Ravi Patel (due 2026-06-04).

Open questions / risks:
- Risk: unknown interaction with 3rd-party telemetry agent causing delayed reboots on some a100-80 nodes. Mitigation: test agent off on 10% canaries.
- Question: do we parallelize firmware micro-patch and driver update, or sequence them? Proposed: sequence (driver then firmware) to limit blast radius.

Appendix — quick run commands (examples):
- Mark cell: infra-cli cells mark --cell us-west1-c2 --state maintenance --owner @ava
- Drain instance: infra-cli instance drain --id i-0abcd --grace 120
- Apply driver image: infra-cli host apply-image --host h-22 --image prepatch-2026-06-driver-528.45
- Restore snapshot: infra-cli host restore --host h-22 --snapshot prepatch-2026-06-01

Notes: This is a working doc. Additions and experiment notes are expected — please append comments inline. If you are an on-call engineer for the windows listed above, mark availability in the calendar and confirm via the #infra-maintenance channel.
